# Results — Study 455 (Rising/Falling Three Methods)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **the
three small candles are a pause, and the breakout confirms the trend continues** — encoded as a
mechanical rule. Five *closed* candles: a long anchor candle, three small candles held inside
its range (10% wick tolerance), then a long candle closing past the anchor in the same
direction. Rising → long, falling → short; entered at the **next close** (one documented lag),
forward return signed by direction over 5/10/20/60 days. Offline & deterministic once cached;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **44** mechanical three-methods patterns pooled across the 5 tapes (~36% rising/long) |
| Timing / costs | five closed candles (no look-ahead); enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per trade |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. This is a single-instrument candlestick study, not a cross-sectional
> anomaly, so survivorship affects only the drift baseline — which the random-entry control
> (matched count *and* long/short mix) neutralizes.

## The signal — three-methods vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the per-pattern mean vs zero; the **Welch pattern-vs-random** *t* (random
entries with the same long/short mix) is the test that matters. Δ = pattern − random. A
*continuation* edge needs the Welch *t* to be **positive and ≥ 2**.

| horizon | n | pattern | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (pattern−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 44 | +9.4 bps  | 55% | +0.27 | −4.7 bps  | **+14.1 bps** | +7.4 bps   | +0.33 | 0.741 |
| 10-day | 44 | +1.5 bps  | 43% | +0.02 | −10.1 bps | **+11.6 bps** | −0.5 bps   | +0.19 | 0.848 |
| 20-day | 44 | −152.9 bps | 36% | −1.92 | +34.3 bps | **−187.3 bps** | −154.9 bps | **−2.50** | **0.015** |
| 60-day | 44 | −106.0 bps | 43% | −0.80 | +129.5 bps | **−235.5 bps** | −108.0 bps | −1.62 | 0.111 |

Read it carefully. There is **no horizon where the pattern beats random**. At 5/10 days the
delta is mildly positive but the Welch *t* is a rounding error (+0.33, +0.19). The *only*
horizon that clears |2| is **20 days, where the Welch *t* is −2.50 (*p* = 0.015) — the pattern
does significantly *worse* than random**. The signed three-methods return at 20 days is
**negative** (−152.9 bps): instead of continuing, the trend tends to give back the breakout.
That is the opposite sign of a continuation edge.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — no coherent edge

| ticker | entries (L/S) | pattern | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (pattern−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 9 (3/6)  | −52.3 bps  | −0.62 | +69.5 bps | **−121.8 bps** |
| QQQ | 12 (4/8) | −309.7 bps | −5.22 | −1.9 bps  | **−307.8 bps** |
| IWM | 7 (2/5)  | −591.2 bps | −5.36 | +76.6 bps | **−667.8 bps** |
| DIA | 7 (3/4)  | −44.1 bps  | −0.44 | +104.5 bps | **−148.6 bps** |
| GLD | 9 (4/5)  | +211.8 bps | +2.14 | −77.0 bps | **+288.7 bps** |

Only **GLD** shows a positive delta (+288.7 bps, on 9 trades); the four equity tapes are all
negative. With 7–12 patterns per name these are tiny samples — the one positive name is noise,
not a cross-sectional edge.

## Geometry placebo — scramble the pattern, nothing changes

The decisive "does the shape matter?" test: fire the same **count** and **long/short mix** on
random calendar dates, destroying the five-candle geometry while keeping the price marginal. If
continuation lived in the shape, the scramble would collapse the result.

| test | observed 20d signed return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY shuffled-date three-methods | −52.3 bps | **0.539** | 500 |

**54% of scrambled-date runs match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.539). The specific
five-candle shape carries no information — random dates do just as well. "The breakout forecasts
continuation" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real continuation

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* post-pause continuation (knob `edge`), the same rule
behaves exactly as it must — so the flat/negative real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there",
not a dead detector.

| planted edge | n | pattern | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no continuation) | 17 | +84.1 bps | 47% | +0.88 |
| **1.00** (real planted continuation) | 19 | +229.2 bps | 68% | **+3.36** |

With no planted continuation the control sits at *t* = +0.88 (no false positive); a real planted
continuation lights up at *t* = +3.36 with a 68% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The three-methods trade does **not** beat a drift- and mix-matched random
  baseline (Δ = +14.1 / +11.6 / −187.3 / −235.5 bps at 5/10/20/60 days). No positive Welch *t*
  reaches 2; the only significant result is **−2.50 at 20 days** — the pattern *loses* to
  random, the wrong sign for a continuation claim.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Only 44 patterns in 21 years, a signed forward return that is flat
  at short horizons and negative at 20 days, and a loss to random entries — there is no edge to
  scale and costs only deepen the hole.
- **"Does the consolidation forecast continuation?" — BUSTED.** The shuffled-date placebo leaves
  the result intact (*p* = 0.539), and over 20 days the trend *gives back* the breakout. The
  pause does not predict the resumption; the three-methods is a descriptive candlestick label,
  not a forecasting strategy.
